blocks.title: Final check
blocks.text: Narrowing is the compiler reading the same runtime checks a human reads. For any union you write: can I name the tag, switch on it exhaustively, and does adding a member break the build everywhere it should? An assertion silences the compiler; a guard convinces it.

caption.text: Part 2 of TS NARROWING. TypeScript's union types are useless until you can prove which member you're holding — and `as` is a lie, not a proof. This field guide walks every guard the compiler actually understands: typeof and its null trap, instanceof and its cross-realm failures, discriminated unions, your own predicates and asserts signatures, and never for compile-time exhaustiveness. 10 pages of dense notes, including the places where narrowing silently breaks and a closing cheat sheet.
